title: 1 in 3 Gen Z Now Lean on AI for Companionship
dek: A Gallup study of 15,925 young people links AI companions to loneliness.

caption:
Your kid's closest confidant might be a chatbot. 🤖

A new global survey from Gallup and the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children's Hospital found that 33% of young people ages 15 to 22 rely on AI for social connection. Among daily AI users, that jumps to 50%. Researchers polled 15,925 Gen Z respondents across 16 countries.

The catch: those leaning on AI companions or online-only friends may face higher odds of loneliness. The researchers stress it's a link, not proof of cause, so it's unclear whether lonely teens turn to tools like ChatGPT or whether AI deepens the isolation. In-person friendships still scored highest for support and wellbeing.

With Australia, the UK and New York tightening rules on youth online safety and AI chatbots, this data lands at a key moment. We're tracking the story at AI Parabellum. Would you notice if a chat turned from homework help into emotional support?

post_caption:
Half of young people who use AI every day now treat it as a friend, not just a tool.

The Gallup and Boston Children's Hospital study of nearly 16,000 Gen Z respondents ties AI companionship to higher loneliness odds, while real-world friends still offer the strongest support. A second phase of the research is planned for spring 2027.
